title: The Philippines did not deliver a South China Sea Code of Conduct. But it has shown what ASEAN can achieve
gist: As 2026 ASEAN Chair, the Philippines failed to conclude a South China Sea Code of Conduct (about 80% of provisions agreed) but set up Singapore, the 2027 chair, to finish it, while concluding the binding ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement. Chatham House argues ASEAN's value lies in incremental integration rather than grand dealmaking, with new faultlines on AI alliances, critical minerals and energy resilience ahead.

themes.theme: South China Sea Code of Conduct

insights.claim: The South China Sea Code of Conduct (COC) was not concluded at the November 2026 ASEAN summit; Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro said around 80 per cent of provisions are agreed but 'sticking points' remain.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: No binding maritime rules yet; Philippines-China coast guard clashes remain an unresolved tail risk.
insights.quote: around 80 per cent of the provisions are agreed

insights.claim: Under Philippine chairmanship, COC delegations met every month in 2026 and produced a substantial part of an agreement, which Chatham House calls a significant jump after two decades of diplomatic deadlock.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Diplomatic momentum on the COC is real, lowering odds of escalation-by-default over time.
insights.quote: a significant jump after two decades of diplomatic deadlock

insights.claim: Past statements suggest the remaining COC sticking points concern legal implementation, geographical scope and terms of reference.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Legal enforceability and scope are the core issues; a COC lacking them would be weak for de-risking maritime trade.

insights.claim: Singapore, the 2027 ASEAN chair, has a more stable relationship with Beijing than Manila and may stand a better chance of finalising the COC, though this remains uncertain.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: 2027 is the next window for a COC; watch Singapore's chairmanship agenda.

insights.claim: The Philippines' deepening treaty alliance with the US under President Marcos and its increasingly fractious relationship with China, a stance not shared by all ASEAN members, impeded its ability to broker the COC as Chair.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Alignment of a mediator with one great power reduces its brokering capacity; divergent ASEAN stances on China persist.

insights.claim: Philippine ships continued to clash with Chinese Coast Guard vessels throughout 2026 around disputed areas such as Scarborough Shoal.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Ongoing maritime incidents are a persistent flashpoint for regional shipping and US-China tension.

insights.claim: Manila concluded negotiations on the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA), described as the world's first binding region-wide digital economy deal, promising $2 trillion by 2030 through cross-border data flows and end-to-end digital trade.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Supports Southeast Asian digital trade, payments and data-center plays as cross-border data flows liberalise.
insights.quote: the world’s first binding region-wide digital economy deal

insights.claim: The Philippines championed the ASEAN Leaders' Declaration on Strategic Trade Management to establish unified frameworks strengthening regional supply chain resilience.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Signals ASEAN alignment on export-control/strategic-trade frameworks relevant to supply-chain relocation.

insights.claim: A new ASEAN free trade agreement with Canada was agreed at the summit, and Brazil and Canada committed $540 million for rainforest protection; more than 150 outcome documents were approved.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Canada-ASEAN FTA opens a new trade corridor amid shifting global trade rules.

insights.claim: ASEAN made little progress on Myanmar: the summit agreed only to 'calibrated engagement' under the '5 Point Consensus', and as a unified group ASEAN appears to have little hope of influencing Myanmar's military government.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Myanmar remains a governance and sanctions risk with no regional resolution in sight.
insights.quote: ASEAN appears to have little hope of influencing Myanmar’s military government

insights.claim: Chatham House argues grand international dealmaking like the COC may continue to prove difficult for ASEAN, but the bloc provides an indispensable function facilitating interoperability and integration that fuels growth and secures sovereignty.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Price ASEAN as an incremental economic integrator, not a security guarantor.

insights.claim: The Marcos administration recorded its lowest ever approval ratings in November 2026, amid energy supply strains from the war in Iran, summer tsunami and earthquake losses, and impeachment proceedings against the Vice President.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Rising Philippine political risk; energy-import vulnerability to Middle East conflict is a macro headwind.
insights.quote: The Marcos administration received its lowest ever approval ratings this month

insights.claim: The war in Iran has strained energy supply chains for the Philippines, hindering access to necessities.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Energy-importing Southeast Asian economies are exposed to Middle East supply shocks.

insights.claim: The ASEAN summit sidelines saw the Quad convene for the first time in two years and Japan's PM Takaichi and South Korea's President Lee Jae Myung hold their fourth bilateral meeting, with Trump, Modi, Carney and Lula attending.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Quad revival signals renewed Indo-Pacific coordination relevant to China risk pricing.
insights.quote: the Quad convened for the first time in two years

insights.claim: Chatham House warns ASEAN must be seen as a key player in its own right rather than a platform through which bilateral deals are done, and Marcos's 'whole-of-ASEAN approach' is a strategy to protect the Philippines amid geopolitical trends.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Fragmentation of ASEAN into bilateral channels would weaken the bloc's collective bargaining with great powers.

insights.claim: In 2027 under Singapore's chairmanship, ASEAN is set to be tested by deepening faultlines on AI alliances, critical mineral exploration, and supply chain and energy resilience, with divergences already appearing among members.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Expect intra-ASEAN divergence on AI and critical minerals alignment with US vs China; country-level dispersion in policy risk.
insights.quote: deepening faultlines on AI alliances, critical mineral exploration, and supply chain and energy resilience
